# AI Engineering Compiler v0.5.0

0.4.0 made Codex and Cursor say, on every run, when they cannot enforce a
declared deny rule, and made `--strict` fail on it. That is the right default,
and it left no way to keep `--strict` once you had read the warning and decided
to live with the gap. This release adds one.

## Accept a gap, per target

```yaml
# .ai/manifest.yaml
targets:
  codex:
    enabled: true
    accept: [permissions-unsupported]
```

In a blueprint, the same list goes under `ai.accept.codex`.

- The diagnostic keeps its code and still prints on every run, as info marked
  accepted (`accepted: true` in `--json`). `--strict` no longer fails on it.
- Only capability gaps can be accepted: `capability-unsupported`,
  `permissions-unsupported`, `sandbox-unsupported`. Anything else, such as a
  hand-edited settings entry, is an error.
- Acceptance applies to the one target that names it. A Cursor target in the
  same workspace still warns.
- A code a target accepts but never reports warns as `accept-unused`, so an
  acceptance cannot outlive its reason.

## This repository uses it

Its own manifest now denies the agent's file tools any read of `.env`,
`.env.*`, `*.pem`, and `*.key`, and accepts the Codex gap, so CI stays on
`--strict`. `aie audit` on this repository is down to one finding: the sandbox
is not enabled.

## Upgrading

No action needed. Workspaces that do not use `accept` behave exactly as in
0.4.0.
